# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence Reviewed
Single artifact: `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory — all findings below come directly from packet analysis with `tshark`.

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** | DHCP, NBNS, all malicious sessions |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** | DHCP Request (frames 1/3) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** | DHCP hostname option, NBNS name registration |
| NetBIOS/AD alias | WIN11OFFICE (domain WIN11OFFICE.COM) | NBNS, Kerberos realm |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos AS/TGS exchanges between 10.1.21.58 and DC 10.1.21.2 (CNameString `gwyatt`, realm `WIN11OFFICE.COM`) |

Domain controller for context: 10.1.21.2 / WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com (not itself compromised evidence-wise).

## 2. Malware Family

**Attribution: behavioral only, NOT signature-confirmed.** No AV/IDS alert file was provided, and no plaintext payload binary was recoverable from the capture (all payload delivery occurred over TLS).

Traffic behavior is consistent with a **browser-fingerprinting "gate" feeding a commodity stealer-as-a-service C2** (the fingerprint-collection JS + `set_agent`/`act=log` check-in pattern is characteristic of Lumma/Vidar/Rhadamanthys-class stealer infrastructure, but I cannot confirm the exact family without an external hash/signature lookup, which was out of scope here). Treat the family name as **unconfirmed — classify only as "generic information-stealer with browser-fingerprinting C2 gate."**

Behavioral evidence supporting this classification:
- A plaintext HTTP page served from the C2 runs full browser/device fingerprinting (navigator properties, WebGL, Canvas, AudioContext, WebRTC ICE candidates, installed fonts, hardware concurrency) and POSTs the result back to `/api/set_agent?...&act=log`.
- The victim is issued a persistent bot ID and token, reused across repeated short-lived TLS beacons to the same C2 IP.
- One beacon session uploaded ~1.48 MB from host→C2 over TLS (frame set 10.1.21.58:61834↔153.92.1.49:443, T+118.3s), consistent with stealer-log/credential exfiltration.
- The C2 itself references per-victim payload archives named `<public-IP>-<hash>.zip`, i.e. server-side packaging keyed to the victim, a pattern typical of stealer log collection panels.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Infection-chain domains/IPs (in time order from capture start)
| T+ (sec) | Domain | Resolved IP(s) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45.35 | `hiyter.com` | 104.21.22.231, 172.67.207.145 (Cloudflare) | Initial redirector/landing (TLS only, content not visible) |
| 45.92 | `media.megafilehub4.lat` | 104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67 (Cloudflare) | Fake file-host stage |
| 48.36 | `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` | 104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13 (Cloudflare) | **Payload delivery** — single TLS session transferred **~16 MB host-inbound** (content encrypted; filename/hash not recoverable from this capture) |

### Command-and-control / exfiltration
| T+ (sec) | Domain | IP:port | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 90.37 | `whooptm.cyou` | **62.72.32.156:443** | Short TLS beacon |
| 92.3–122.8 | `whitepepper.su` | **153.92.1.49:443** and **153.92.1.49:80** | Primary C2. Many repeated short TLS beacons on :443 (~20–40 frames each, ~0.7–2.8s duration) plus plaintext HTTP fingerprint gate on :80. One :443 session at T+118.3s pushed ~1.48 MB client→server (likely stolen-data exfil). |
| 122.8 | `holiday-forever.cc` | **80.97.160.24:443** | TLS beacon |
| 126.5 | `communicationfirewall-security.cc` | **104.21.9.36:443**, 172.67.141.109 | Two TLS sessions, ~102 KB and ~34 KB host-inbound |

### Malicious URLs (plaintext, decrypted from HTTP on whitepepper.su:80)
```
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log   (POST, x-www-form-urlencoded, ~8 KB fingerprint payload)
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log
http://whitepepper.su/favicon.ico
```
Bot ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
Session token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

### File/archive references
- Server-side response text (from whitepepper.su, plaintext) references a per-victim archive:
  `172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip`
  — the trailing token is 32 hex chars (MD5-length, **not SHA256**), and the request for this archive itself failed server-side ("cant open archive ..."). No archive bytes were transferred in the clear, so **no SHA256 of any transferred file can be computed from this capture.**
- The 16 MB payload fetched from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` was entirely TLS-encrypted; its file name and hash are not recoverable without a TLS key log, which was not provided.

## Notes / Excluded Noise
Background traffic to Microsoft (`login.live.com`, `*.data.microsoft.com`, NCSI), Google (`clients*.google.com`, `safebrowsing.google.com`, `mtalk.google.com`), Bing, and Skype/Office endpoints is normal Windows/Edge/Chrome telemetry and was excluded from the IOC list.

## Recommended Actions
- Isolate DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (10.1.21.58) from the network immediately; treat user `gwyatt`'s credentials as compromised (reset AD password, revoke sessions).
- Block/sinkhole: `whitepepper.su`, `whooptm.cyou`, `holiday-forever.cc`, `communicationfirewall-security.cc`, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, `media.megafilehub4.lat`, `hiyter.com` and their resolved IPs at perimeter/DNS.
- Acquire the host's disk/memory for offline malware identification (the pcap alone cannot yield a definitive family name or file hash — TLS blocks payload inspection).
- Assume browser-stored credentials/cookies/autofill data were exfiltrated given the ~1.48 MB upload to the C2; force credential rotation for accounts used on this workstation.
